title: Ēsh ismak? A classmate from Jeddah
goal: At university, a new Saudi classmate from Jeddah asks you for yesterday's lecture notes; catch his Saudi forms and ask him to slow down
tip: Saudi speakers from Jeddah say some everyday words differently. Learn to hear them, and keep your own: ēsh = shu 'what', abgha = abi 'I want', daḥḥīn = il-ḥīn 'now', īwa = hē 'yes', marra ḥilu = wāyid ḥilu 'really nice'. If it's too fast: ma lḥigt ʿalēk.
grammar: recycle; listening to other Gulf voices (receptive)
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم. أنا تركي، من جدة. إيش اسمك؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. ana Turki, min Jidda. ēsh ismak?
Hi. I'm Turki, from Jeddah. What's your name?
B
وعليكم السلام. أنا سالم. تشرفنا
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. ana Sālim. tsharrafna
Hello. I'm Sālim. Nice to meet you.
A
الشرف لي. أبغى منك خدمة، عندك ملاحظات المحاضرة؟ أنا ما جيت أمس
ish-sharaf li. abgha minnak khidma, ʿindak mulāḥaẓāt il-muḥāẓra? ana ma jīt ams
Likewise. Can you do me a favour: have you got the lecture notes? I didn't come yesterday.
B
هيه، عندي. تبيها الحين؟
hē, ʿindi. tabīha l-ḥīn?
Yes, I have. Do you want them now?
A
إيوه، دحين لو تقدر، عشان عندي اختبار بكرة الصبح
īwa, daḥḥīn lō tigdar, ʿashān ʿindi ikhtibār bukra ṣ-ṣubḥ
Yes, now if you can, because I've got a test tomorrow morning.
B
السموحة، تكلم على راحتك. ما لحقت عليك
is-samūḥa, tkallam ʿala rāḥtak. ma lḥigt ʿalēk
Sorry, take it slowly. I didn't catch that.
A
ما عليه. يعني الحين، الاختبار بكرة
ma ʿalēh. yaʿni l-ḥīn, il-ikhtibār bukra
No problem. I mean now: the test is tomorrow.
B
آه، فهمت. بطرش لك الصور الحين
āh, fhimt. baṭarrish-lak iṣ-ṣuwar il-ḥīn
Ah, I get it. I'll send you the photos now.
A
مشكور يا سالم! خطك حلو، والملاحظات مرة حلوة. الله يعطيك العافية
mashkūr yā Sālim! khaṭṭak ḥilu, w il-mulāḥaẓāt marra ḥilwa. allāh yaʿṭīk il-ʿāfya
Thanks, Sālim! Your handwriting's nice, and the notes are really good. Thanks a lot.
B
الله يعافيك. وإذا احتجت أي شي، أنا حاضر
allāh yʿāfīk. w idha ḥtajt ay shay, ana ḥāẓir
You're welcome. And if you need anything, I'm happy to help.
items: to a woman: ēsh ismik?; UAE: shismak? (شسمك؟); (recognise)
can you do me a favour? (lit. I want a favour from you) (Saudi)
UAE: abi minnak khidma (أبي منك خدمة); (recognise)
UAE: il-ḥīn; you'll also hear daḥīn and dalḥīn; (recognise)
UAE: wāyid ḥilu; marra here means 'very', not 'once'; (recognise)
do you want it now? (a feminine thing or plural things) (to a man)
to a woman: tabīnha l-ḥīn? (تبينها الحين؟)
a test: ikhtibār; an exam: imtiḥān
I didn't catch that, I couldn't keep up with you (to a man)
to a woman: ma lḥigt ʿalēch
culture: Saudi Arabia has several big dialect groups. Jeddah, Mecca and Medina, in the west, speak Hijazi: ēsh 'what', abgha 'I want', daḥīn 'now', īwa 'yes'. Riyadh and the centre speak Najdi, and the Eastern Province speaks a Gulf dialect close to Kuwaiti and Bahraini.

title: Penalty! A match on TV
goal: At Sēf's place, watch the second half of a league match with him: follow the score, the referee and the commentator
tip: Recycle the past for what just happened: sajjalaw gōl 'they scored', ṭāḥ 'he went down', ma ʿaṭāh 'he didn't give it'. TV commentators often use fuṣḥā-flavoured words like ẓarbat jazāʼ 'penalty kick'; people at home just say bilanti.
grammar: recycle: past tense for events (sajjalaw, ṭāḥ, ma ʿaṭāh)
dialogue: A
تعال بسرعة! بدا الشوط الثاني، والنتيجة واحد واحد
taʿāl b-surʿa! bida sh-shōṭ ith-thāni, w in-natīja wāḥid wāḥid
Come quick! The second half's started, and it's one all.
B
أوه! منو سجل الهدف حقنا؟
ōh! minu sajjal il-hadaf ḥaggna?
Oh! Who scored our goal?
A
اللاعب اليديد، بالراس. بس هم سجلوا هدف قبله من بلنتي
il-lāʿib il-yidīd, bir-rās. bas hum sajjalaw hadaf gablah min bilanti
The new player, with a header. But they scored before that, from a penalty.
B
بلنتي؟ الحكم هذا دايما ضدنا
bilanti? il-ḥakam hādha dāyman ẓiddna
A penalty? This referee's always against us.
A
شوف شوف! طاح داخل المنطقة!
shūf shūf! ṭāḥ dākhil il-manṭiga!
Look, look! He's gone down in the box!
B
والحكم ما عطاه شي! مية بالمية بلنتي
w il-ḥakam ma ʿaṭāh shay! miya bil-miya bilanti
And the referee's given him nothing! That's a penalty, a hundred percent.
A
اسمع المعلق، يقول ضربة جزاء واضحة والحكم ما شافها
ismaʿ il-muʿalliq, ygūl ẓarbat jazāʼ wāẓḥa w il-ḥakam ma shāfha
Listen to the commentator: he says it's a clear penalty and the referee didn't see it.
B
خف شوي يا ريّال، هد أعصابك. باقي ربع ساعة
khiff shwayy yā rayyāl, hidd aʿṣābak. bāgi rubʿ sāʿa
Ease off a bit, man, calm down. There's a quarter of an hour left.
A
هدف! سجلنا! اثنين واحد!
hadaf! sajjalna! thnēn wāḥid!
Goal! We've scored! Two-one!
B
ما قلت لك؟ هد أعصابك وبنفوز
ma gilt-lak? hidd aʿṣābak w binfūz
What did I tell you? Calm down and we'll win.
items: the first half: ish-shōṭ il-awwal (الشوط الأول)
we scored: sajjalna; you'll also hear the English gōl
in the box, inside the (penalty) area
calm down, keep your cool (to a man)

title: Don't spoil it for me!
goal: In a university corridor, Sēf asks if you've finished the Kuwaiti series he told you about; talk about the episodes, the actors and the next season
tip: Recycle bāgi-li for what's left: bāgi-li thalāth ḥalgāt 'I've got three episodes left'. And the future b- for what's coming: biyinzil 'it'll come out', bashtirik 'I'll subscribe'. To stop a spoiler: la tḥarrig ʿalay!
dialogue: A
خلصت المسلسل الكويتي اللي قلت لك عنه؟
khallaṣt il-musalsal il-kwēti illi gilt-lak ʿannah?
Have you finished the Kuwaiti series I told you about?
B
للحين، باقي لي ثلاث حلقات
lil-ḥīn, bāgi-li thalāth ḥalgāt
Not yet, I've got three episodes left.
A
لا تفوت الحلقة الأخيرة! النهاية...
la tfawwit il-ḥalga l-akhīra! in-nihāya…
Don't miss the last episode! The ending…
B
لا لا، لا تحرق علي!
la la, la tḥarrig ʿalay!
No, no, don't spoil it for me!
A
هههه ما بقول شي. بس الممثلين وايد زينين فيه، مية بالمية
hahaha, ma bagūl shay. bas il-mumaththilīn wāyid zēnīn fīh, miya bil-miya
Ha ha, I won't say a thing. But the actors are really good in it, a hundred percent.
B
صح، والحلو فيه اللهجة. للحين أتعلم منها
ṣaḥḥ, w il-ḥilu fīh il-lahja. lil-ḥīn atʿallam minha
True, and the good thing about it is the dialect. I'm still learning from it.
A
زين. والموسم الثاني بينزل السنة الياية، هذا كلام الناس
zēn. w il-mōsim ith-thāni biyinzil is-sana l-yāya, hādha kalām in-nās
Good. And the second season's coming out next year, that's what people are saying.
B
صج؟ وين بيعرضونه؟
ṣij? wēn biyʿarẓūnah?
Really? Where are they going to show it?
A
على نفس المنصة، بس لازم تشترك عشان تشوفه. الاشتراك على قد الحال
ʿala nafs il-minaṣṣa, bas lāzim tishtirik ʿashān tshūfah. il-ishtirāk ʿala gadd il-ḥāl
On the same platform, but you have to subscribe to watch it. The subscription doesn't cost much.
B
عجبتني الفكرة. بشترك ونشوفه سوا
ʿajbatni l-fikra. bashtirik w nshūfah sawa
I like the idea. I'll subscribe and we'll watch it together.
items: the last episode, the final episode
don't spoil it for me (to a man)
to a woman: la tḥarrgīn ʿalay
they'll show it, they'll air it (a masculine thing)
you have to subscribe (to a man)
task: This week: Dubai is full of Egyptian and Levantine Arabic. Search YouTube for «مسلسل سوري» (Syrian series) or «فيلم مصري» (Egyptian film) and watch 5 minutes. Note 3 words that aren't Gulf (Egyptian izzayyak 'how are you', Levantine kīfak, shū), then tell Sēf in Gulf Arabic what happened in the clip.

title: Wish raʼyak? A fan from Riyadh
goal: At a café showing a match, the Saudi fan from Riyadh at the next table starts chatting about football; catch his Najdi forms and tell him who you support
tip: Riyadh speech has its own words, too: wish 'what' (wish raʼyak? 'what do you think?'), wājid 'very' (UAE wāyid), shāhi 'tea' (UAE chāy), and the greeting kēf ḥālak? Answer in your own Gulf forms: he'll understand you.
grammar: recycle; listening to other Gulf voices (receptive)
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم. كيف حالك؟ الكرسي هذا فاضي؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. kēf ḥālak? il-kursi hādha fāẓi?
Hello. How are you? Is this chair free?
B
وعليكم السلام. بخير الله يسلمك. تفضل
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. b-khēr allāh ysallmak. tfaẓẓal
Hello. Fine, thanks. Go ahead.
A
مشكور. وش رايك في المباراة؟ الشوط الثاني بدا، والفريقين واجد زينين
mashkūr. wish raʼyak fi l-mubārā? ish-shōṭ ith-thāni bida, w il-farīgēn wājid zēnīn
Thanks. What do you think of the match? The second half's started, and both teams are really good.
B
صح، بس الدفاع حقهم ضعيف. والحكم بعد!
ṣaḥḥ, bas id-difāʿ ḥagghum ẓaʿīf. w il-ḥakam baʿad!
True, but their defence is weak. And so is the referee!
A
معك حق. وانت، أي فريق تشجع؟
maʿak ḥagg. w inta, ay farīg tshajjiʿ?
You're right. And you: which team do you support?
B
أشجع فريق من لندن، وفي الإمارات أشجع فريق ربيعي
ashajjiʿ farīg min Landan, w fi l-imārāt ashajjiʿ farīg rbīʿi
I support a London team, and in the Emirates I support my friend's team.
A
زين! تبي شاهي؟ أنا بطلب لي واحد
zēn! tabi shāhi? ana baṭlub-li wāḥid
Nice! Do you want some tea? I'm going to order one for myself.
B
لا، مشكور. عندي كرك
la, mashkūr. ʿindi karak
No, thanks. I've got a karak.
A
شوف الهجمة! واجد حلوة، بس ضيعها
shūf il-hajma! wājid ḥilwa, bas ẓayyaʿha
Look at that attack! Really nice, but he wasted it.
B
خسارة! كانت فرصة ذهبية
khasāra! kānat furṣa dhahabiyya
What a shame! It was a golden chance.
items: to a woman: kēf ḥālik?; UAE: shḥālak?; (recognise)
what do you think? (Saudi) (to a man)
to a woman: wish raʼyik?; UAE: shrāyak?; (recognise)
which team do you support? (to a man)
to a woman: ay farīg tshajjʿīn?
a golden chance, a great chance
culture: Saudi speech is not one accent. Najdi, from Riyadh and the centre, has wish for 'what'; Hijazi, from Jeddah, has ēsh. Saudis say shāhi for 'tea', and kēf ḥālak? is an everyday Saudi greeting, not just fuṣḥā. Asking 'what do you want?' straight out (ēsh tabgha?) isn't rude there: it means 'what can I do for you?'

title: A Qatari on the project
goal: At university, plan a group project with a Qatari classmate: split the work, set a deadline, and catch his Qatari forms
tip: Qatari speech is close to Emirati, but you'll hear humma for 'they' and huwwa for 'he' (UAE hum, huwa), and shinu for 'what', as in Kuwait. Recycle kill wāḥid 'each one' to split the work: kill wāḥid yākhidh juzʼ.
grammar: recycle; listening to other Gulf voices (receptive)
dialogue: A
هلا سالم. الدكتور قال لازم نسلم المشروع الأحد
hala Sālim. id-daktōr gāl lāzim nsallim il-mashrūʿ il-aḥad
Hi Sālim. The professor said we have to hand the project in on Sunday.
B
هلا فيك. الأحد؟ يعني باقي لنا أسبوع
hala fīk. il-aḥad? yaʿni bāgi-lna usbūʿ
Hi. Sunday? So we've got a week left.
A
زين. شنو رايك نقسم الشغل بيننا؟
zēn. shinu raʼyak ngassim ish-shughul bēnna?
Good. What do you think about splitting the work between us?
B
عجبتني الفكرة. كل واحد ياخذ جزء
ʿajbatni l-fikra. kill wāḥid yākhidh juzʼ
I like the idea. Each of us takes a part.
A
والثنين الباقيين؟ هم قالوا بيكتبون المقدمة
w ith-thnēn il-bāgyīn? humma gālaw biyiktibūn il-mugaddima
And the other two? They said they'll write the introduction.
B
زين. وأنا باخذ الأرقام والرسوم
zēn. w ana bākhidh il-argām w ir-rusūm
Fine. And I'll take the figures and the charts.
A
وأنا العرض. بس هو قال لازم نتدرب عليه قبل
w ana l-ʿarẓ. bas huwwa gāl lāzim nitdarrab ʿalēh gabil
And I'll do the presentation. But he said we need to practise it beforehand.
B
خلاص، نتقابل في المكتبة يوم الخميس
khalāṣ, nitgābal fi l-maktaba yōm il-khamīs
OK, let's meet in the library on Thursday.
A
تمام. وإذا احتجت أي شي، طرش في القروب
tamām. w idha ḥtajt ay shay, ṭarrish fi l-grūb
Fine. And if you need anything, post in the group.
B
إن شاء الله. يلا، نشوفك الخميس بعد العصر
in shāʼ allāh. yalla, nshūfak il-khamīs baʿd il-ʿaṣir
Will do. Right, see you Thursday, late afternoon.
items: post it in the group (chat) (to a man)
to a woman: ṭarrshi fi l-grūb
culture: Gulf Arabic, the family Emirati belongs to, is spoken in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE and eastern Saudi Arabia. Each country's speech has its own marks: Qatari humma 'they', Kuwaiti shinu and iḥna, Bahraini āni 'I' in some communities. Oman has its own dialects, and many Omanis say ج as g.

title: His voice is beautiful
goal: In Sēf's car, he plays a song by a Khaleeji singer; talk about the voice, the words and the tune, and plan to go to his concert
tip: Recycle comparisons and 'the best thing about it': ṣōtah aḥla min…, il-ḥilu fīha il-kalimāt. Use ʿala bāli 'I thought' to say what you expected: ʿala bāli kalimātha ṣaʿba.
grammar: recycle: comparatives, il-ḥilu fīha, ʿala bāli
dialogue: A
اسمع هالأغنية! هذي أحلى أغنية عنده
ismaʿ hal-ughniya! hādhi aḥla ughniya ʿindah
Listen to this song! This is his best song.
B
منو المطرب؟ صوته حلو وايد
minu l-muṭrib? ṣōtah ḥilu wāyid
Who's the singer? His voice is really beautiful.
A
مطرب إماراتي. الحلو فيها الكلمات واللحن
muṭrib imārāti. il-ḥilu fīha l-kalimāt w il-laḥan
An Emirati singer. The best thing about it is the words and the tune.
B
على بالي الكلمات صعبة، بس فهمت أكثرها
ʿala bāli l-kalimāt ṣaʿba, bas fhimt aktharha
I thought the words would be hard, but I understood most of them.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! هذي أغنية قديمة، من التسعينات. أيام أول!
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! hādhi ughniya gadīma, min it-tisʿīnāt. ayyām awwal!
Well done you! This is an old song, from the nineties. The old days!
B
وعنده أغاني يديدة؟
w ʿindah aghāni yidīda?
And has he got new songs?
A
هيه، ونازل له ألبوم يديد. وبيسوي حفلة في دبي الشهر الياي
hē, w nāzil-lah albōm yidīd. w biysawwi ḥafla fi Dbayy ish-shahar il-yāy
Yes, he's got a new album out. And he's doing a concert in Dubai next month.
B
يلا نروح! بحجز تذاكر من الحين
yalla nrūḥ! baḥjiz tadhākir min il-ḥīn
Let's go! I'll book tickets right now.
A
تراها بتخلص بسرعة، الكل يبي يحضر
tarāha bitkhallaṣ b-surʿa, il-kill yabi yiḥẓar
They'll sell out fast, you know; everyone wants to go.
B
خلاص، حطها علي. وانت اختار المقاعد
khalāṣ, ḥuṭṭha ʿalay. w inta khtār il-magāʿid
OK, leave it to me. And you choose the seats.
items: his voice is beautiful, he's got a lovely voice
the words and the tune, the lyrics and the melody
he'll do a concert, he'll put on a show
everyone wants to go, everyone wants to be there

title: Tell us about yourself
goal: In a job interview for a graduate post at a Dubai company, answer the HR manager's first questions about you and your experience
tip: At an interview, talk in polite Gulf Arabic with some formal work words: khibra 'experience', taḥt iẓ-ẓaghiṭ 'under pressure'. Answer about yourself with the present: adris handasa 'I study engineering', ashtaghil zēn… 'I work well…'.
grammar: recycle; office register (polite, more formal words)
dialogue: A
حياك الله. تفضل استريح
ḥayyāk allāh. tfaẓẓal istirīḥ
Welcome. Please, have a seat.
B
الله يحييك. مشكور على الفرصة
allāh yḥayyīk. mashkūr ʿala l-furṣa
Thank you. Thanks for the opportunity.
A
العفو. خبرنا عن نفسك شوي
il-ʿafu. khabbirna ʿan nafsak shwayy
Not at all. Tell us a bit about yourself.
B
أدرس هندسة، وأتدرب في شركة في دبي من سنتين
adris handasa, w atdarrab fi sharika fi Dbayy min santēn
I study engineering, and I've been an intern at a company in Dubai for two years.
A
زين. وليش تبي تشتغل عندنا بالذات؟ مب بس عشان الراتب؟
zēn. w lēsh tabi tishtaghil ʿindana bidh-dhāt? mub bas ʿashān ir-rātib?
Good. And why do you want to work for us in particular? Not just for the salary?
B
لا، بالعكس. شركتكم معروفة، وأبي أتعلم أكثر
la, bil-ʿaks. sharikatkum maʿrūfa, w abi atʿallam akthar
No, not at all. Your company is well known, and I want to learn more.
A
حلو. وشو نقاط القوة عندك؟ خبرني بصراحة
ḥilu. w shu nuqāṭ il-quwwa ʿindak? khabbirni b-ṣarāḥa
Nice. And what are your strengths? Tell me honestly.
B
أشتغل زين تحت الضغط، وأحب الشغل ويا الفريق
ashtaghil zēn taḥt iẓ-ẓaghiṭ, w aḥibb ish-shughul wiyya l-farīg
I work well under pressure, and I like working with the team.
A
ممتاز. وشو خبرتك في البرامج؟ في السيرة الذاتية مكتوب وايد
mumtāz. w shu khibratak fi l-barāmij? fi s-sīra dh-dhātiyya maktūb wāyid
Excellent. And what's your experience with software? Your CV lists a lot.
B
عندي خبرة سنتين فيها، وأتعلم بسرعة
ʿindi khibra santēn fīha, w atʿallam b-surʿa
I've got two years' experience with them, and I learn fast.
items: thanks for the opportunity (to a man)
to a woman: mashkūra ʿala l-furṣa
tell us about yourself (to a man)
to a woman: khabbrīna ʿan nafsich
why do you want to work for us? (to a man)
to a woman: lēsh tabīn tishtaghlīn ʿindana?
your company is well known (to a group)
you'll also hear the English: is-sī vī; (recognise)

title: Where do you see yourself?
goal: In the second half of the interview, talk about a weakness and your plans, ask your own questions, and find out what happens next
tip: Recycle atmanna for hopes: atmanna akūn masʼūl ʿan… 'I hope to be in charge of…'. Polite closing lines matter as much as answers: mashkūr ʿala wagtak 'thanks for your time'. idha ṣār naṣīb 'if it's meant to be' keeps you modest.
grammar: recycle; office register (polite, more formal words)
dialogue: A
وشو نقاط الضعف عندك؟
w shu nuqāṭ iẓ-ẓaʿf ʿindak?
And what are your weaknesses?
B
أحيانا أدقق في التفاصيل وايد، وآخذ وقت
aḥyānan adaggig fi t-tafāṣīl wāyid, w ākhidh wagt
Sometimes I focus too much on the details, and I take time.
A
هذا مب عيب. ووين تشوف نفسك بعد خمس سنين؟
hādha mub ʿēb. w wēn tshūf nafsak baʿd khams snīn?
That's not a bad thing. And where do you see yourself in five years?
B
أتمنى أكون مسؤول عن مشاريع كبيرة
atmanna akūn masʼūl ʿan mashārīʿ kbīra
I hope to be in charge of big projects.
A
إن شاء الله. عندك أي سؤال لنا؟
in shāʼ allāh. ʿindak ay suʼāl lana?
I hope so. Have you got any questions for us?
B
هيه. إذا صار نصيب، متى أقدر أبدا؟
hē. idha ṣār naṣīb, mita agdar abda?
Yes. If it works out, when could I start?
A
بعد ما تتخرج. وبنتصل فيك بعد أسبوعين بالكثير
baʿd ma titkharraj. w binittaṣil fīk baʿd usbūʿēn bil-kathīr
After you graduate. And we'll call you in two weeks at the most.
B
زين. وشو الخطوة الياية؟
zēn. w shu l-khaṭwa l-yāya?
Good. And what's the next step?
A
مقابلة ثانية ويا المدير. الله يوفقك
mugābla thānya wiyya l-mudīr. allāh ywaffgak
A second interview with the manager. Good luck.
B
آمين. ومشكور على وقتك
āmīn. w mashkūr ʿala wagtak
Thank you. And thanks for your time.
items: I pay close attention to detail, I check the details
that's not a bad thing, there's nothing wrong with that
where do you see yourself? (to a man)
to a woman: wēn tshūfīn nafsich?
(I) be in charge of, be responsible for (said by a man)
a woman says: akūn masʼūla ʿan
have you got any questions? (to a man)
to a woman: ʿindich ay suʼāl?
if it works out, if it's meant to be
thanks for your time (to a man)

task: This week: in Talk, ask your partner to play an HR manager interviewing you for a job in Dubai. Answer at least 6 questions in Gulf Arabic, and use khabbirna ʿan nafsak, ʿindi khibra, taḥt iẓ-ẓaghiṭ and wēn tshūf nafsak in the conversation. Ask two questions of your own, and close with mashkūr ʿala wagtak. Then do it again, faster.

title: The job offer
goal: The company's HR manager phones with a job offer; thank him, ask politely for a higher salary, and ask for time to think
tip: Asking for more, politely: mumkin tzīdūn ir-rātib shwayy? 'could you raise the salary a little?', then give a reason. Recycle aqall min 'less than' and the -ūn ending for 'you' (the company): tzīdūn, ʿalēkum.
grammar: recycle; office register (polite, more formal words)
dialogue: A
مبروك يا سالم! عندنا لك عرض شغل
mabrūk yā Sālim! ʿindana lak ʿarẓ shughul
Congratulations, Sālim! We've got a job offer for you.
B
الله يبارك فيك! والله ما توقعتها بهالسرعة
allāh ybārik fīk! wallāh ma twaggaʿtha b-has-surʿa
Thank you! Honestly, I didn't expect it so soon.
A
الراتب الأساسي في الإيميل، وفوقه بدل سكن ومواصلات
ir-rātib il-asāsi fi l-īmēl, w fōgah badal sakan w muwāṣalāt
The basic salary's in the email, and on top of it there's a housing and transport allowance.
B
زين. بس الراتب أقل من اللي توقعته
zēn. bas ir-rātib aqall min illi twaggaʿtah
Good. But the salary's less than I expected.
A
هذا راتب الخريجين عندنا، والزيادة على حسب الأداء
hādha rātib il-khirrījīn ʿindana, w iz-ziyāda ʿala ḥasab il-adāʼ
That's our graduate salary, and raises depend on performance.
B
فاهم. بس ممكن تزيدون الراتب شوي؟ عندي خبرة سنتين
fāhim. bas mumkin tzīdūn ir-rātib shwayy? ʿindi khibra santēn
I understand. But could you raise the salary a little? I've got two years' experience.
A
ما أقدر أوعدك بشي، بس بكلم المدير
ma agdar awʿidak b-shay, bas bakallim il-mudīr
I can't promise you anything, but I'll talk to the manager.
B
مشكور. وأقدر أفكر فيه كم يوم؟
mashkūr. w agdar afakkir fīh cham yōm?
Thanks. And can I think about it for a few days?
A
أكيد. بس رد علينا قبل نهاية الأسبوع
akīd. bas rudd ʿalēna gabil nihāyat il-usbūʿ
Of course. But get back to us before the end of the week.
B
إن شاء الله، برد عليكم قبل الخميس
in shāʼ allāh, barudd ʿalēkum gabil il-khamīs
Will do. I'll get back to you before Thursday.
items: I didn't expect it so soon (a feminine thing)
a masculine thing: ma twaggaʿtah b-has-surʿa
could you raise the salary a little? (to a group, a company)
هل يمكن أن تزيدوا الراتب قليلًا؟
to one man: mumkin tzīd ir-rātib shwayy?
I can't promise you anything (to a man)
to a woman: ma agdar awʿidich b-shay
can I think about it? (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: agdar afakkir fīha?
before the end of the week

title: As you can see on the slide
goal: Present your part of the project to Bū Saʿīd and the team: introduce it, walk them through the slides and take questions
tip: Talking to a group, use the -ūn and -kum forms: mithil ma tshūfūn 'as you can see', idha ʿindakum ay suʼāl 'if you have any questions'. Order your points: awwal shay… w thāni shay… 'first… and second…', and sum up with b-ikhtiṣār 'in short'.
grammar: recycle; office register (polite, more formal words)
dialogue: A
يلا يا سالم، الكل موجود. تفضل
yalla yā Sālim, il-kill mawjūd. tfaẓẓal
Right, Sālim, everyone's here. Go ahead.
B
مشكور. خلوني أبدا بفكرة المشروع
mashkūr. khallūni abda b-fikrat il-mashrūʿ
Thank you. Let me start with the idea behind the project.
A
تفضل، كلنا آذان صاغية
tfaẓẓal, killna ādhān ṣāghya
Go ahead, we're all ears.
B
مثل ما تشوفون في الشريحة، الطلبات زادت هالسنة
mithil ma tshūfūn fi sh-sharīḥa, iṭ-ṭalabāt zādat has-sana
As you can see on the slide, orders have gone up this year.
A
زين. وشو السبب؟
zēn. w shu s-sabab?
Good. And what's the reason?
B
سببين. أول شي التطبيق اليديد، وثاني شي الأسعار
sababēn. awwal shay it-taṭbīq il-yidīd, w thāni shay il-asʿār
Two reasons. First, the new app, and second, the prices.
A
واضح. والشريحة الياية؟
wāẓiḥ. w ish-sharīḥa l-yāya?
Clear. And the next slide?
B
باختصار، اقتراح الفريق إننا نوسع الخدمة لأبوظبي
b-ikhtiṣār, iqtirāḥ il-farīg innana nwassiʿ il-khidma l-Abuẓabi
In short, the team's suggestion is that we expand the service to Abu Dhabi.
A
فكرة حلوة. نحتاج أرقام أكثر، بس العرض ممتاز
fikra ḥilwa. niḥtāj argām akthar, bas il-ʿarẓ mumtāz
Good idea. We need more figures, but the presentation is excellent.
B
زين، بطرش لكم الأرقام باكر. وإذا عندكم أي سؤال، أنا موجود
zēn, baṭarrish-lkum il-argām bāchir. w idha ʿindakum ay suʼāl, ana mawjūd
OK, I'll send you the figures tomorrow. And if you have any questions, I'm here.
items: with the idea of the project
as you can see (to a group)
to one man: mithil ma tshūf
you'll also hear the English: is-slāyd
orders have gone up, requests have increased
the team's suggestion, the team's proposal

title: Can I have a word?
goal: Go to your manager, Bū Saʿīd, with a complaint: files from another department keep reaching you late; raise it respectfully and ask for a solution
tip: To complain upwards, open softly and stay calm: ṭāl ʿumrak, mumkin ākhidh min wagtak digīgtēn? Say the problem without blaming anyone: ma abi ashtiki ʿala ḥad, bas… and ask for a fix: abi nilga ḥall.
grammar: recycle; office register (polite, more formal words)
dialogue: A
هلا سالم، تفضل. خير؟
hala Sālim, tfaẓẓal. khēr?
Hi Sālim, come in. What's up?
B
طال عمرك، ممكن آخذ من وقتك دقيقتين؟
ṭāl ʿumrak, mumkin ākhidh min wagtak digīgtēn?
Sir, could I take two minutes of your time?
A
أكيد، تفضل. شو عندك؟
akīd, tfaẓẓal. shu ʿindak?
Of course, go ahead. What is it?
B
بصراحة، الشغل صاير وايد علي هالأيام
b-ṣarāḥa, ish-shughul ṣāyir wāyid ʿalay hal-ayyām
Honestly, I've got too much work on these days.
A
ليش؟ شو اللي تغير؟
lēsh? shu illi tghayyar?
Why? What's changed?
B
الملفات توصلني متأخرة من القسم الثاني، وأقعد للمسا
il-milaffāt tōṣalni mitʼakhkhra min il-gism ith-thāni, w agʿid lil-misa
The files reach me late from the other department, and I stay till the evening.
A
من متى هالشي؟ ليش ما قلت لي من قبل؟
min mita hash-shay? lēsh ma gilt-li min gabil?
Since when? Why didn't you tell me before?
B
ما أبي أشتكي على حد، بس أبي نلقى حل
ma abi ashtiki ʿala ḥad, bas abi nilga ḥall
I don't want to complain about anyone, I just want us to find a solution.
A
كلامك في محله. بكلم رئيس القسم وبنرتب الشغل من جديد
kalāmak fi maḥallah. bakallim raʼīs il-gism w binrattib ish-shughul min jadīd
You've got a point. I'll talk to the head of the department and we'll reorganise the work.
B
مشكور طال عمرك، هذا اللي أبيه
mashkūr ṭāl ʿumrak, hādha illi abīh
Thank you, sir, that's what I'm after.
items: could I take two minutes of your time? (to a man)
هل يمكن أن آخذ من وقتك دقيقتين؟
to a woman: mumkin ākhidh min wagtich digīgtēn?
I've got too much work, the work's piling up on me
they reach me late, (it) reaches me late (a feminine thing or plural things)
I don't want to complain about anyone
لا أريد أن أشتكي على أحد
you've got a point, what you say is right (to a man)
to a woman: kalāmich fi maḥallah; (recognise)

title: Office or majlis?
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, tell him about your job offer and hear his advice on talking at work and in the majlis
tip: The same person talks differently at the office and in the majlis. At work: shu l-akhbār?, ṭāl ʿumrak, short and to the point. In the majlis: start with the greeting, ask shu ʿilūmak? 'what's your news?', and let the older man lead.
grammar: recycle: register and address (office vs majlis)
dialogue: A
سمعت إنهم عطوك عرض شغل! مبروك يا ولدي
simaʿt innhum ʿaṭūk ʿarẓ shughul! mabrūk yā wildi
I hear they've offered you a job! Congratulations, son.
B
الله يبارك فيك يا عمي. للحين ما رديت عليهم
allāh ybārik fīk yā ʿammi. lil-ḥīn ma raddēt ʿalēhum
Thank you, uncle. I haven't answered them yet.
A
لا تطول عليهم، الفرص ما تنتظر حد
la tṭawwil ʿalēhum, il-furaṣ ma tintiẓir ḥad
Don't keep them waiting; chances don't wait for anyone.
B
صح. بس أبي أتعلم كيف أتكلم في الشغل
ṣaḥḥ. bas abi atʿallam chēf atkallam fi sh-shughul
True. But I want to learn how to talk at work.
A
في الشغل الكلام رسمي أكثر. المدير تقول له طال عمرك، مب يا ريّال
fi sh-shughul il-kalām rasmi akthar. il-mudīr tgūl-lah ṭāl ʿumrak, mub yā rayyāl
At work the talk is more formal. You call the manager 'sir', not 'mate'.
B
وفي المجلس؟ أقدر أسولف براحتي؟
w fi l-majlis? agdar asōlif b-rāḥti?
And in the majlis? Can I chat freely?
A
هيه، بس الكبير له احترامه. تبدا بالسلام وتسأل عن العلوم
hē, bas il-kbīr lah iḥtirāmah. tibda bis-salām w tisʼal ʿan il-ʿilūm
Yes, but the older man gets his respect. You start with the greeting and ask after the news.
B
تسلم يا عمي على النصيحة
tislam yā ʿammi ʿala n-naṣīḥa
Thanks for the advice, uncle.
A
الله يسلمك. يعني في المجلس شو علومك، وفي الشغل شو الأخبار. وبتعرف السنع يا ولدي
allāh ysallmak. yaʿni fi l-majlis shu ʿilūmak, w fi sh-shughul shu l-akhbār. w bitaʿarf is-sanaʿ yā wildi
You're welcome. So in the majlis it's 'what's the news?', and at work 'what's the latest?'. And you'll learn good manners, son.
B
كله منكم يا عمي. وباكر برد عليهم إن شاء الله
killah minkum yā ʿammi. w bāchir barudd ʿalēhum in shāʼ allāh
It's all thanks to you, uncle. And tomorrow I'll give them my answer, God willing.
items: I haven't answered them yet, I haven't got back to them yet
don't keep them waiting (to a man)
to a woman: la tṭawwlīn ʿalēhum
(I) chat freely, talk as I like
the older man gets his respect, elders are respected
what's your news? how are things? (majlis) (to a man)
it's all thanks to you (to a group or, respectfully, to one person)
culture: Emiratis move between registers every day. Everyday life is in Emirati Arabic, formal settings such as the news, speeches and education use fuṣḥā, and many workplaces also run in English. Sanaʿ is the Emirati word for the inherited code of manners and behaviour that shapes the majlis, a part of Emirati identity built on mutual respect.

title: Checkpoint 4.5: I got the job!
goal: Checkpoint: Fahad phones from Kuwait; tell him about the job offer, the interview and the salary talk, and catch his Kuwaiti forms
tip: Review, and now you say it: ʿarẓ shughul, ʿindi khibra, taḥt iẓ-ẓaghiṭ, mumkin tzīdūn ir-rātib shwayy?, idha ṣār naṣīb, ma lḥigt ʿalēk and hidd aʿṣābak. Fahad uses Kuwaiti forms (shinu, iḥna, ḥēl).
grammar: checkpoint 4.5 (s4u058–s4u069): other Gulf voices, media, interviews and office register
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟ وشنو أخبار المقابلة؟
hala wallāh! shlōnak? w shinu akhbār il-mugābla?
Hey! How are you? And what news of the interview?
B
هلا فيك! الحمد لله، عطوني عرض شغل!
hala fīk! il-ḥamdu lillāh, ʿaṭūni ʿarẓ shughul!
Hi! Great, thanks: they've offered me a job!
A
مبروك! حيل فرحت لك. شنو سألوك؟
mabrūk! ḥēl firaḥt lak. shinu saʼlūk?
Congratulations! I'm really happy for you. What did they ask you?
B
الله يبارك فيك. سألوني عن خبرتي، وقلت أشتغل زين تحت الضغط
allāh ybārik fīk. saʼlūni ʿan khibrati, w gilt ashtaghil zēn taḥt iẓ-ẓaghiṭ
Thank you. They asked about my experience, and I said I work well under pressure.
A
زين قلت! والراتب؟ إحنا في الكويت نقول الراتب أهم شي
zēn gilt! w ir-rātib? iḥna fi l-Kwēt ngūl ir-rātib ahamm shay
Well said! And the salary? In Kuwait we say the salary's the most important thing.
B
طلبت منهم يزيدون الراتب شوي
ṭalabt minhum yzīdūn ir-rātib shwayy
I asked them to raise it a little.
A
حركات! وإذا ما وافقوا؟
ḥarakāt! w idha ma wāfagaw?
Smart move! And if they don't agree?
B
عادي، بقبل إذا صار نصيب. أهم شي الخبرة
ʿādi, bagbal idha ṣār naṣīb. ahamm shay il-khibra
That's fine, I'll accept if it works out. Experience is what matters most.
A
كلامك صح. ولازم نحتفل لما أيي دبي
kalāmak ṣaḥḥ. w lāzim niḥtifil lamma ayi Dbayy
You're right. And we must celebrate when I come to Dubai.
B
أكيد! بس هد أعصابك في المباراة
akīd! bas hidd aʿṣābak fi l-mubārā
Definitely! But keep your cool at the match.
items: what news of the interview? how did the interview go? (Kuwait)
I'm really happy for you (Kuwait) (to a man)
to a woman: ḥēl firaḥt lich; UAE: wāyid firaḥt lak; (recognise)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search «معلم لهجة إماراتية» or «Emirati Arabic tutor»), tell the story of a job interview, real or imagined: the questions, your answers, the salary talk. Use 4 items from these two weeks, e.g. khabbirna ʿan nafsak, ʿindi khibra, taḥt iẓ-ẓaghiṭ, idha ṣār naṣīb. Let your partner ask follow-up questions for 8 turns.
